title: Sell Mineral Rights in Alpine, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Alpine, WY | Lincoln County
metaDescription: Own a mineral interest near Alpine, WY at the head of the Overthrust Belt? I'll check county records and give you a straight number before you consider selling.
heroLead: Alpine sits where three rivers meet at the northern edge of Lincoln County, and it's grown a lot as a resort town, but the mineral estate under most of that ground was severed off long before the first cabin went up.
intro: I've worked Lincoln County deed books for years, and the pattern up here is consistent: a family homesteaded, an oil company leased the minerals sometime in the 60s, 70s, or 80s, the lease expired without a well, and the severed interest just sat there through however many owners the surface has had since. That's most of what I find tied to Alpine addresses.
If you're holding one of those interests, or you inherited a fraction and don't know what county unit it's even in, I'll pull the record and tell you honestly what you've got.

sections.heading: Where Alpine sits in the play
paragraphs: The Overthrust Belt's productive fields, Fontenelle, Whitney Canyon, Carter Creek, sit south and east of here. Alpine is near the trend's edge, so activity has historically been leasing rather than drilling. That matters because it puts most Alpine-area minerals in the undeveloped, speculative category rather than the currently-producing one.
It doesn't make the interest worthless. It just means the price reflects potential, not a royalty stream, and I quote it that way.

sections.heading: Sorting out ownership after resort growth
paragraphs: Alpine's population has grown fast with second homes and short-term rentals, and that surface turnover can make people assume their mineral rights transferred with a property sale. Usually they didn't. If your family held the original ranch or homestead ground, there's a good chance the mineral estate is still sitting with you or your relatives, untouched by whoever bought the surface lot.

sections.heading: Getting a real number
paragraphs: I check the Lincoln County recorder for lease history on your specific section, confirm your fractional share against the deed chain, and price against recent comparable trades in the area, not a flat rate that ignores your actual position.

faqs.question: Is my Alpine mineral interest connected to Jackson Hole activity?
faqs.answer: No, Jackson Hole and Teton County have almost no oil and gas leasing due to federal land restrictions. Alpine's minerals relate to the Overthrust Belt trend to the south, a separate geologic story.

faqs.question: What if I don't have the original deed?
faqs.answer: I can usually reconstruct your ownership from the Lincoln County recorder's index using your name or your relative's name.

faqs.question: Does a resort development on the surface affect my mineral value?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly, through access considerations. The mineral estate itself is valued on geology and lease history, not surface development.

faqs.question: How quickly can I get an actual number?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days of getting your deed or probate information.
